statement: A `regular` portion is ALWAYS an officially published standard portion (TÜBER). `small` and `large` are product-derived reference sizes unless an official source publishes them explicitly. Derived values must never be presented as published values; every derived row carries the derivation in `transformation_notes`. v2 adds the `unit_multiple` source for foods eaten in discrete units — half an egg or 0.65 of a slice of bread is not a portion, it is an artefact of multiplying a factor.

dairy_cheese.rationale: Cheese is served in fingers/matchbox units; 5 g steps keep the derived sizes on a realistic breakfast plate.

dairy_yogurt.rationale: Bowl fill level scales continuously; 10 g steps avoid implying weighing precision the reference photo cannot support.
dairy_yogurt.bandExemption: smallFactor 0.625 is below the 0.60-0.70 band floor by design: it lands on 150 g, the ~small-bowl fill that reads clearly against the 240 g cup portion.

grain_cooked.smallPublishedRule: TÜBER Ek 2.1.5 footnote 4 — one standard portion of rice/bulgur/pasta is the GARNISH serving; the second-course serving eaten at home equals 2 standard portions. `small` therefore uses the published 1-portion garnish weight and `regular` uses the published 2-portion serving weight.
grain_cooked.rationale: Both small and regular are published by TÜBER; only `large` is product-derived.

legume_cooked.rationale: Ladle-served; 5 g steps match the 2-küçük-kepçe household measure TÜBER prints.

meat_cooked.rationale: Cooked meat portions are palm-sized units; 50 g reads as a half palm against the published 80 g palm portion.
meat_cooked.bandExemption: smallFactor 0.625 is below the 0.60-0.70 band floor by design so the derived weight lands on 50 g rather than 52.5 g.

vegetable_cooked.rationale: Ladle- or spoon-served; 10 g steps match how a cooked vegetable is portioned onto a plate.

vegetable_raw.rationale: Salad-style serving; the same spread as cooked, but plated rather than ladled.

fruit_whole.rationale: Fruit is eaten in whole pieces. Half a piece and two pieces are real servings; 0.65 of an apple is not.

dried_fruit.rationale: Handful-served and energy-dense, so the band is much tighter than fresh fruit.

bread.rationale: TÜBER publishes bread as slices/pieces (Simit 50 g, Yufka 50 g); halves and doubles keep that unit intact.

egg_unit.rationale: TÜBER publishes 100 g = 2 medium eggs, so the unit is 50 g. small=1 egg, large=3.

nuts_seeds.rationale: TÜBER publishes 30 g (1 avuç). Energy-dense, so the absolute band stays small.

fish_cooked.bandExemption: smallFactor 0.625 is below the 0.60-0.70 floor by design: against the published 150 g it lands on 95 g, a realistic single fillet.
fish_cooked.rationale: Portioned as fillets or whole small fish.

fat_oil.rationale: Spoon-measured and extremely energy-dense; the band exists to stop an implausible derived weight reaching the UI.

beverage_dairy.bandExemption: smallFactor 0.625 matches dairy_yogurt: against the published 240 mL cup it lands on 150 g, a small glass.

sizeSources.published: The size is printed by TÜBER; used verbatim.
sizeSources.factor: Derived by multiplying the published regular weight by the category factor, inside derivedFactorBands.
sizeSources.unit_multiple: Derived as a whole- or half-unit multiple of the published unit weight, for discrete foods.
